chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from al-Fudayl from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:
"The woman prays behind her husband the obligatory prayer and the voluntary prayer, and follows him in the prayer."
ai.seo_question: Does a wife pray behind her husband in both obligatory and voluntary prayers?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the domestic structure of congregational prayer, affirming the wife’s role as a follower (ma'mum) to her husband in both obligatory and voluntary prayers. This ruling underscores the hierarchical yet cooperative nature of the family unit in Shia jurisprudence, where the husband’s leadership in prayer mirrors his broader spiritual and domestic authority.
